title: Derived etale cohomology over an inverse limit
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$ be a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated $T$-schemes with affine transition maps and limit $Y$, and let $K\in D^+(\Ab(T_{\Et}))$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] be a bounded-below complex of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write $K_i$ and $K_Y$ for its derived inverse images [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] on $Y_i$ and $Y$. Then the pullback maps induce, for every integer $n$, an isomorphism

$$
 \varinjlim_i H^n(Y_{i,\Et},K_i)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^n(Y_{\Et},K_Y),
$$

where cohomology of a complex is the cohomology of derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No torsion or fixed finite coefficient-ring hypothesis is required.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0GIT (lemma-colimit-complexes), lines 7852-7881: continuity of etale cohomology for bounded-below complexes over a qcqs inverse system with affine transition maps

proof.text: Represent $K$ by a complex $C^\bullet$ of abelian sheaves, using the localization description of the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Since $K\in D^+$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], choose $a$ with $H^r(C^\bullet)=0$ for $r<a$. Replace $C^\bullet$ by the good truncation $G^\bullet=\tau_{\geq a}C^\bullet$: it is zero below $a$, has $G^a=\operatorname{coker}(C^{a-1}\to C^a)$, and agrees with $C^\bullet$ above $a$. The quotient map $C^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ induces an isomorphism on $H^r$ for $r\geq a$, and both sides have zero $H^r$ for $r<a$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism and $G^\bullet$ represents $K$. No injectivity or acyclicity of the terms of $G^\bullet$ is asserted.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0GIT (lemma-colimit-complexes), proof lines 7867-7869; bounded-below replacement spelled out

proof.text: For each $i$ and for $Y$, pull $G^\bullet$ back termwise to $F_i^\bullet$ and $F_Y^\bullet$. The derived inverse-image definition [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] says these complexes represent $K_i$ and $K_Y$, without requiring their terms to be injective. The transition maps are the inverse-image composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], degree by degree and compatible with differentials. After pulling to $Y$, every $f_i^{-1}F_i^r$ identifies with the same sheaf $F_Y^r$; the transition maps become identities. The connected filtered-diagram colimit statement [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram] therefore identifies $\varinjlim_i f_i^{-1}F_i^\bullet$ with $F_Y^\bullet$ termwise. Every $F_i^r$ is zero for $r<a$ because inverse image preserves zero objects.

The system $(F_i^\bullet)$ satisfies the uniform lower bound and all the transition and affine-limit hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-complex-systems] (Stacks 0EZM). Apply that lemma in degree $n$ and use the termwise colimit identification of Step 2 to obtain $\varinjlim_iH^n(Y_{i,\Et},F_i^\bullet)\cong H^n(Y_{\Et},F_Y^\bullet)$. Here $H^n$ means cohomology of derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]; 0EZM uses $H^t(Y_i,F_i^s)$ in all degrees $t$ to obtain this conclusion. No termwise global-sections complex is claimed to compute these groups.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0GIT (lemma-colimit-complexes), proof lines 7870-7874; Lemma Tag 0EZM, lines 7783-7823

proof.text: The identifications $F_i^\bullet\simeq K_i$ and $F_Y^\bullet\simeq K_Y$ from Step 2 replace the two sides of Step 3 with the groups in the statement. The map supplied by 0EZM is induced by the projection pullbacks and the colimit coprojections, so under those natural identifications it is precisely the displayed canonical map.
